title: Agile in projects and in business as usual
blurb: Explain how agile is used both in business as usual and in projects, and what makes a project different from BAU.
question: A customer-service team already handles its daily requests with Kanban. It now needs a new self-service portal built by staff from several departments over nine months. Which work is business as usual, which is a project, and where does PRINCE2 Agile fit?

teach.body: Agile is used in two settings. In business as usual (BAU), teams run and improve ongoing products and services, often with Scrum or Kanban. In projects, temporary teams introduce a change. PRINCE2 Agile is designed for projects: it wraps agile delivery in project direction and management. Agile in BAU carries on before and after a project, as ongoing product work.

teach.loop: BAU runs in its new form

teach.body: A project is a temporary organization created to deliver one or more products according to an agreed business case. BAU identifies the need for change; the project is the means by which that change is introduced. When the project ends, BAU adopts the new products and the benefits that flow from them.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1; PRINCE2 7 definition of a project

rows.label: Temporary
values: Has a start and an end

teach.caption: The Agile book's 1.3.1 names five characteristics that set a project apart from BAU; the fifth, uncertainty, is listed in PRINCE2 7.

teach.h: Is this BAU or a project?

teach.body: Once a project hands over, the product lives on in BAU. PRINCE2 Agile describes agile product management: a high-level product vision with a flexible roadmap, short cycles prioritized by value and feedback, and close collaboration. Further enhancements are handled through these product management iterations rather than by starting a new project for each one.

teach.h: One product, BAU and a project

items.label: BAU team runs the old service with Kanban
PRINCE2 Agile project builds the new portal

teach.body: Larkfield Water's customer-service team handles billing queries with a Kanban board: that is agile in BAU. The company then needs a smart-meter portal, built by IT, billing and field staff over nine months. That temporary, cross-functional change is a project, run by project manager Daniel Mensah with PRINCE2 Agile. After handover, the service team's product backlog absorbs new enhancements in regular iterations.

teach.text: Agile is not limited to projects, and a project is not 'BAU in sprints'. A project is temporary and introduces change; BAU is ongoing. Small enhancements after handover go through product management iterations, not a new project each time.

items: Agile runs in BAU (ongoing product work) and in projects; PRINCE2 Agile is for projects.
A project is the means by which change is introduced into BAU.
Project characteristics: change, temporary, cross-functional, unique (plus uncertainty in PRINCE2 7).
After handover, enhancements continue through agile product management iterations.

summary: You can now explain how agile works in both BAU and projects, and why projects are the means of introducing change into BAU. You can also tell project work from BAU using the characteristics of change, temporary, cross-functional and unique.

A.q: What is the relationship between projects and business as usual (BAU)?
options: Projects are the means of introducing change into BAU
BAU is the means of introducing change into projects
Projects replace BAU permanently once they close
Projects and BAU are the same kind of ongoing work
A.why: BAU identifies a need for change and a project introduces it; afterwards BAU adopts the change (1.3.1).

whyNot.1: This reverses the relationship: projects introduce change into BAU.
whyNot.2: Projects are temporary; BAU continues in its new form after they close.
whyNot.3: BAU is ongoing and repetitive; projects are temporary and unique.

A.q: A project has a defined start and end, after which BAU takes over the change and its benefits. Which project characteristic is this?
A.why: Temporary means a project has a start and an end, after which BAU adopts the change and the benefits (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Unique is about a different team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe.
whyNot.2: Cross-functional is about teams spanning divisions or organizations.
whyNot.3: Change is about the project introducing what BAU has identified as needed.

A.q: Can agile ways of working be used in business as usual?
options: No, agile belongs to projects and not to BAU
Yes, but each piece of BAU work must become a project
No, BAU work must follow a linear-sequential method
Yes, agile also supports ongoing BAU product work
A.why: Agile is used in BAU as well as in projects; PRINCE2 Agile focuses on the project setting (1.1).

whyNot.0: Agile is widely used in BAU, for example Kanban for ongoing service requests.
whyNot.1: BAU work does not need to be turned into a project to use agile.
whyNot.2: Nothing requires BAU to be linear-sequential; many BAU teams work in an agile way.

B.q: A council has run several library refurbishments, but each one involves a different building, contractor and timeframe. Which project characteristic does this illustrate?
B.why: Unique means each project differs in some way, such as team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe, even if similar projects have gone before (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Temporary is about having a start and an end.
whyNot.1: Cross-functional is about people from different functions working together.
whyNot.3: Change is about introducing what BAU needs, not about each project being different.

B.q: A project team brings together IT, finance and frontline staff from different divisions. Which project characteristic is this?
B.why: Cross-functional means project teams span functional divisions and sometimes organizations (1.3.1).

whyNot.1: Unique is about the project differing from others, not about who is on the team.
whyNot.2: Temporary is about the project having a start and an end.
whyNot.3: Uncertainty is about the extra threats and opportunities projects face.

B.q: After a PRINCE2 Agile project closes, users ask for a series of small enhancements to the product. How does PRINCE2 Agile suggest they are handled?
options: By starting a new project for each one
By reopening the closed project's last stage
By asking the former project board to approve each
B.why: Enhancements after the project are handled through agile product management iterations, not a new project each time (14.2.2.1).

whyNot.0: A new project for every small enhancement is what the book advises against.
whyNot.2: A closed project is not reopened; the product continues in BAU.
whyNot.3: The project board ceases to exist when the project closes.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. BAU work is repetitive and ongoing.
2. A project is a permanent part of the organization.
3. PRINCE2 Agile focuses on using agile within projects.
4. Agile ways of working cannot be used outside projects.
C.why: BAU is repetitive and ongoing (1), and PRINCE2 Agile is designed for agile within projects (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: a project is temporary.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: projects are temporary, and agile is used in BAU too.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: agile is also used in business as usual.

C.q: A housing charity's operations team handles routine tenancy queries with Kanban. The charity now needs a new tenant portal, built over nine months by staff from IT, finance and housing. Which statement is correct?
options: Both are projects, because both use agile
Both are BAU, because the charity runs them
The queries are a project; the portal is BAU
The queries are BAU; the portal is a project
C.why: Routine queries are ongoing, repetitive BAU work; the portal is a temporary, cross-functional change, so it is a project suited to PRINCE2 Agile.

whyNot.0: Using agile does not make work a project; agile is used in BAU too.
whyNot.1: The portal is temporary and introduces change, so it is a project.
whyNot.2: This reverses the two: the ongoing queries are BAU and the portal is the project.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Business as usual identifies the need for change, and a [?] is the means by which that change is introduced.
C.why: A project is the means by which change is introduced into BAU (1.3.1).

whyNot.1: A process is a set of activities within PRINCE2, such as 'starting up a project'.
whyNot.2: A practice is an aspect managed throughout a project, such as risk or progress.
whyNot.3: A principle is a guiding obligation, such as 'manage by stages'.

reteach.title: Running the shop and refitting it
reteach.question: What is the difference between running a shop and refitting it?

blocks.body: Running a shop every day (serving customers, restocking shelves) is BAU: ongoing and repetitive. Refitting the shop is a project: it has a start and an end, brings in different skills, is unlike previous refits and introduces change. Once the refit is done, the shop goes back to BAU in its new form. Either kind of work can be done in an agile way.

blocks.text: Agile does not turn BAU into a project. Ask: is it temporary and does it introduce change? If yes, it is a project.

explain.body: BAU identifies the need for change; a project introduces it; then BAU adopts the change and its benefits (1.3.1).

test.q: Which statement best describes the purpose of a project in relation to BAU?
options: To run BAU services more cheaply each year
To replace the BAU teams on a permanent basis
To keep BAU services working unchanged
To introduce a change that BAU needs
test.why: Projects are the means by which change is introduced into BAU (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Running services is BAU's own job, not the project's purpose.
whyNot.1: BAU continues after the project, in its new form.
whyNot.2: A project exists to change BAU, not to keep it the same.

explain.body: Change, temporary, cross-functional and unique (1.3.1), with uncertainty as the fifth in PRINCE2 7. BAU, by contrast, is ongoing and repetitive.

test.q: Which characteristic says that a project differs in some way from others, for example in its team, customer or location?
test.why: Unique means each project has something different: team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Temporary concerns the start and end of a project.
whyNot.1: Cross-functional concerns people from different functions working together.
whyNot.3: Change concerns introducing what BAU needs.

explain.body: Agile is not just for projects. BAU teams use agile frameworks such as Scrum or Kanban to run and improve products and services continually (1.1).

explain.caption: A BAU team's Kanban board for ongoing requests.

test.q: A payroll team uses a Kanban board to handle its continual stream of queries. How should this be classified?
options: Agile used in business as usual
A PRINCE2 Agile project in delivery
test.why: Ongoing, repetitive query handling is BAU, and Kanban is an agile way of running it (1.1).

whyNot.1: There is no temporary change being introduced, so it is not a project.
whyNot.2: It is neither a project nor linear-sequential.
whyNot.3: A programme coordinates related projects; this is routine BAU work.

explain.body: After handover, agile product management keeps the product evolving: a flexible roadmap, short value-driven cycles, and enhancements through product iterations rather than new projects (14.2.2.1).

test.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile describe the handling of product enhancements after a project?
options: A new project for each one
A change request to the old board
An extension to the final stage
test.why: Enhancements are handled through product management iterations, not by starting a new project for each (14.2.2.1).

whyNot.0: The book advises against a new project for every enhancement.
whyNot.2: The project board does not continue after closure.
whyNot.3: The final stage ends with closure; it is not extended for later enhancements.
